Having concluded my observations on our religion, I wish to emphasize the singular and pressing necessity of our time. We owe profound gratitude to Vyâsa, the illustrious author of the Mahâbhârata, for providing this great work during the current Kali Yuga. The rigorous practices of Tapas and other forms of Yoga, which were effective in previous Yugas, are no longer suitable for the present age; instead, the imperative of this era is the act of giving and aiding others.

To clarify the concept of Dana, or charity, it is essential to understand the hierarchy of gifts. The supreme gift is the imparting of spiritual knowledge, followed by the dissemination of secular knowledge, then the preservation of life, and finally, the provision of food and drink. He who imparts spiritual knowledge liberates the soul from the cycle of many births, while he who provides secular knowledge enlightens individuals, guiding them toward spiritual understanding. All other forms of charity, including the saving of life, rank far below these two. Consequently, it is crucial to recognize that the dissemination of spiritual knowledge holds far greater value than any other endeavor, representing the highest and most significant form of assistance.

Our scriptures contain an eternal fountain of spirituality, and no other region on earth offers such noble examples of practical spirituality as this land of renunciation. Based on my experience of the world, I can affirm that while other lands may be filled with discourse, true practical religion—religion integrated into daily life—is found here and here alone. Mere speech does not constitute religion; parrots and machines may speak, but they do not practice. Rather, one must look for a life characterized by renunciation, spirituality, enduring suffering, and infinite love, for such a life is the true mark of a spiritual individual.

Given these ideals and the noble practical examples present in our country, it would be a profound regret if the treasures within the minds and hearts of these great Yogis remained hidden. These insights must be extracted and made the common property of all people, regardless of wealth, poverty, or social status. Furthermore, this knowledge must be disseminated not only within India but broadcast across the entire world, which is one of our most significant duties. You will find that the more you strive to help others, the more you benefit yourselves. Therefore, if you truly love your religion and your country, your vital duty is to strive diligently to bring the treasures from your closed books to their rightful heirs.

I have finished what I had to say about our religion. I will end by reminding you of the one pressing necessity of the day. Praise be to Vyâsa, the great author of the Mahâbhârata, that in this Kali Yuga there is one great work. The Tapas and the other hard Yogas that were practiced in other Yugas do not work now. What is needed in this Yuga is giving, helping others. What is meant by Dana? The highest of gifts is the giving of spiritual knowledge, the next is the giving of secular knowledge, and the next is the saving of life, the last is giving food and drink. He who gives spiritual knowledge, saves the soul from many end many a birth. He who gives secular knowledge opens the eyes of human beings to wards spiritual knowledge, and far below these rank all other gifts, even the saving of life. Therefore it is necessary that you learn this and note that all other kinds of work are of much less value than that of imparting spiritual knowledge. The highest and greatest help is that given in the dissemination of spiritual knowledge. There is an eternal fountain of spirituality in our scriptures, and nowhere on earth, except in this land of renunciation, do we find such noble examples of practical spirituality. I have had a little experience of the world. Believe me, there is much talking in other lands; but the practical man of religion, who has carried it into his life, is here and here alone. Talking is not religion; parrots may talk, machines may talk nowadays. But show me the life of renunciation, of spirituality, of all-suffering, of love infinite. This kind of life indicates a spiritual man. With such ideas and such noble practical examples in our country, it would be a great pity if the treasures in the brains and hearts of all these great Yogis were not brought out to become the common property of every one, rich and poor, high and low; not only in India, but they must be thrown broadcast all over the world. This is one of our greatest duties, and you will find that the more you work to help others, the more you help yourselves. The one vital duty incumbent on you, if you really love your religion, if you really love your country, is that you must struggle hard to be up and doing, with this one great idea of bringing out the treasures from your closed books and delivering them over to their rightful heirs.

Previous research utilizing Rolimeter measurements and other instrumented knee assessment systems has identified potential errors and challenges associated with the standardization of test procedures (Daniel et al., 1985; Hatcher et al., 2005; Muellner et al., 2001). To address these issues, the present study implemented standardized protocols designed to enhance the reproducibility of repeated measurements. Specifically, a leg support attachment was employed with the KT 1000 arthrometer. This device features a rigid leg support and an adjacent footplate equipped with lateral foot stabilization, which maintains consistent leg rotation across multiple measurement sessions. This approach is supported by Fiebert et al. (1994), who reported variations in anterior displacement when KT 1000 measurements were taken at different lower leg rotation angles.

In the current study, the knee support was positioned immediately above the knee flexion crease. This placement prevented the support from exerting anterior translational force on the lower leg, thereby avoiding artificially low displacement values relative to the femur during Rolimeter assessments. Furthermore, maximum force was applied during testing, as previous studies have demonstrated that this method yields more reliable results for both KT 1000 and Rolimeter measurements (Balasch et al., 1999; Panisset et al., 2012; Torzilli et al., 1991; Van Eck et al., 2013).

Procedural precision was maintained by centering the feeler over the tibial tuberosity. The tester’s proximal hand was positioned with the thumb located just distal to the feeler bar on the frame, while the remaining fingers rested on the patellar component of the Rolimeter. This technique ensured stable device positioning, minimizing the risk of medial or lateral sliding that could compromise measurement accuracy. Finally, the distal hand, which applied anterior force to the tibia, was placed with all fingers dorsal to the calf, adhering to recommendations established by Ganko et al. (2000) and Schuster et al. (2004).

Several previous studies involving Rolimeter measurements as well as other instrumented knee measurement systems address the possible errors and difficulties in the standardization of the test procedure (Daniel et al., 1985; Hatcher et al., 2005; Muellner et al., 2001). In the present study, an attempt was made to standardize the test procedure and thereby increase the reproducibility of the repeated measurements; therefore, a leg support to the KT 1000 arthrometer was used. This device has a firm leg support and also an adjacent footplate with a lateral foot support, which helps to keep the rotation of the leg in a more consistent position when making measurements at different time points. Fiebert et al. (1994) found differences in the anterior displacement when measuring with the KT1000, in different rotation positions of the lower leg. In the present study, the knee support was placed just above the fold of the knee to prevent the knee support from putting any anterior translation force to the lower leg and thereby possibly creating a false low displacement value compared to the femur when measuring with the Rolimeter. Maximum force, which has been demonstrated in previous studies to give more reliable results for both the KT 1000 and Rolimeter measurements, was used (Balasch et al., 1999; Panisset et al., 2012; Torzilli et al., 1991; Van Eck et al., 2013). The position of the feeler was also controlled to be centered over the tibial tuberosity. The proximal hand of the tester was placed with the thumb just distally to the feeler bar, on top of the frame, and the other fingers on the patella part of the Rolimeter. This technique was used to control the position of the Rolimeter to avoid the risk of a medial or lateral slide, which would alter the measurement position. The distal hand, creating the anterior force to the tibia was held with all fingers dorsally onto the calf, based on previous recommendations by Ganko et al. (2000) and Schuster et al. (2004).

（二）学法分析 1.体验感悟法：学生通过亲身参与摸球游戏和实验探究活动，直观感受确定事件和不确定事件的特点，体验可能性大小与数量的关系，积累数学活动经验。在体验中理解抽象的概率概念，避免死记硬背结论，实现从体验到理解、从具象到抽象的认知飞跃，契合四年级学生的认知特点。 2.合作探究法：以4人小组为单位，开展合作实验，明确小组分工（操作员、记录员、分析师、汇报员），共同完成实验任务。在小组内，学生分享实验想法、记录实验数据、分析实验结果、讨论存在的问题，互相帮助、互相启发，培养合作意识和合作能力，同时在讨论中深化对知识的理解，突破教学难点，落实吴迪、朱明、黄伟等学者提出的跨学科、小组合作能提升学生综合能力的研究结论。 3.归纳总结法：学生在完成实验、分析数据后，自主归纳实验结论，总结确定事件和不确定事件的定义、可能性大小与数量的关系，将零散的知识系统化、条理化。培养归纳总结能力和逻辑推理能力，实现从具体实验到抽象规律的提升，同时养成探究—分析—归纳的良好数学学习习惯。 五、教学资源整合运用 （一）教学资源整合 实物与教具资源整合：核心是让学生通过具象操作开展实验探究，覆盖游戏—实验—验证全流程。具体会准备透明盒子（每组1个，共8-10组）、不同颜色的乒乓球（红球、白球、黄球若干，数量可灵活调整，如3红1白、5红1白、2红2白等），方便学生直观观察盒子里球的数量和颜色，开展摸球实验；搭配实验记录单（分层设计，基础版、提高版），满足不同层次学生的记录需求；准备彩色马克笔、直尺，方便学生整理数据、绘制简单的统计图；配备磁吸式实验结果展示板，课堂上能直接展示各小组的实验记录和分析结果，及时梳理探究思路，强化知识认知。

(2) 学习分析

体验法与反思法：学生亲身参与摸球游戏和实验探究活动，直接体验必然事件和不确定事件的特点，感受概率大小与数量之间的关系，从而积累数学活动经验。在体验过程中，理解抽象的概率概念，避免机械记忆结论，实现从经验到认识的飞跃，实现由具体到抽象的飞跃，符合四年级学生的认知特点。

合作探究法：学生以四人为一小组进行合作实验，在小组内分工（实验操作员、实验记录员、实验分析员、小组汇报员），合作完成实验任务。在小组内，学生交流实验想法，记录实验数据，分析实验结果，讨论实验中存在的问题，互相帮助，互相启发，培养学生的合作意识和合作能力，加深对知识的理解，克服教学中的难点，落实吴迪、朱明、黄伟等学者关于跨学科合作和小组合作能够提升学生综合能力的科研结论。

归纳法与总结法：在实验完成、数据分析之后，学生独立总结实验结论，定义必然事件、不确定事件以及概率大小与数量之间的关系，从而使零散的知识系统化、条理化。在归纳总结的过程中，培养学生的归纳总结能力和逻辑推理能力，从而实现从具体实验到抽象规律的转化，培养良好的数学学习探究、分析、总结的习惯。

V. 教学资源整合与应用

(1) 教学资源整合

实物与学具的整合：关键在于让学生通过动手操作进行实验探究，贯穿游戏—实验—验证的整个过程。具体来说，准备透明盒子（每组一个，共8~10个小组），不同颜色的乒乓球（如红、白、黄，球的数量可根据实验需要灵活调整，例如3红1白、5红1白、2红2白等）。让学生能够直观地看到盒子中球的数量和颜色，进行摸球实验。提供不同层次的实验记录单（基础层和提高层），满足不同层次学生记录的要求。准备彩笔和尺子，方便学生整理数据，绘制简单的统计图表。配备磁性实验结果展示板，能够将各小组的实验记录和分析结果在课堂上进行集中展示，有利于及时回顾探究思路，巩固知识。

It is instructive to examine the progressive stages of Christ’s service as delineated by the apostle. First, Christ gave Himself for the assembly, dying to possess the Church because He loved it. The fundamental motive for this sacrifice was the love of His heart. While the parable suggests that He desired to purchase the Church, the teaching of Ephesians reveals the secret motive: His love for it. However, His service for the assembly did not conclude with this act. Human devotion can extend no further than dying on behalf of one’s beloved; yet, in death, a person loses all earthly objects. In contrast, Christ died to possess the assembly, and His service for the object of His heart begins precisely where the service of a mere human must end.

Secondly, He sanctifies and cleanses the Church with the washing of water by the word. Although He possessed it through His sacrifice, the Church did not yet meet His desires. It was a pearl in His eyes, but He was required to bring out its beauty, a task accomplished through the application of the Word. Initially, the Church was not His, but He bought it; it was not clean, so He cleansed it; it was not set apart, so He sanctified it. These actions are tokens of His love for His assembly. Ultimately, He will present the assembly to Himself as glorious, without spot or wrinkle or any such defect. This is the end He has in view. The scope of the service He has undertaken and the goal He has proposed for Himself are profound. The delight He will experience when He presents the assembly to Himself, glorious and without blemish, is immeasurable. Throughout this passage, the reader should note that the Church’s joy is not mentioned. Instead, the Holy Spirit delights to dwell on Christ’s love, Christ’s present service, and the end He has in view.

We should mark the progressive stages of His service which the apostle traces out for us. First, Christ gave Himself for the assembly. He died to possess the Church, and that because He loved it. The motive, the reason for thus dying, was simply the love of His heart. The parable tells us He desired to purchase it. The teaching of Ephesians acquaints us with the secret motive—love for it. His service for the assembly did not however end there. Man’s devotedness can proceed no further than to die instead of his object; but in dying, man loses any earthly object. Christ, on the contrary, died to possess the assembly, and His service for the object of His heart begins, where that of a mere man’s must end. So, secondly, He sanctifies it and cleanses it with the washing of water by the word. As first possessed then by Him, it does not answer to that which He desires. A pearl it is in His eyes, but He must bring out its beauty. This He does by the application of the word. Once it was not His, but He bought it. It was not clean, so He would cleanse it. It was not set apart, but He would sanctify it. These are tokens of His love to His assembly. By-and-by He will present the assembly to Himself glorious, not having spot or wrinkle, or any such thing. Such is the end He has in view. What a service has He undertaken! What an end has He proposed to Himself! What delight will He have when He presents the assembly to Himself glorious, without any blemish. Throughout this passage the reader should remark, we have nothing told us of the Church’s joy. Christ’s love, Christ’s present service, the end He has in view, on these points the Holy Ghost delights to dwell.

国内相关研究紧跟教育数字化转型趋势，在政策驱动下快速发展，呈现“技术应用落地快、教学路径探索浅”的特点，研究成果主要集中于政策支持、技术研发与单一功能应用三个方面。 在政策支持与技术研发方面，我国新课标明确提出“推进信息技术与物理教学深度融合”，为AI辅助虚拟仿真实验的发展提供了政策指引[1]。教育部教育技术与资源发展中心牵头开展“虚拟实验教学应用试点”项目，推动AI虚拟实验工具在全国多所高中的试点应用，积累了丰富的实践经验[14]。国内高校与企业合作研发了多款虚拟实验平台，如清华大学的“iLabX”虚拟实验平台、南京师范大学联合企业开发的“AI物理实验助手”，这些平台具备虚拟器材搭建、实验过程仿真、基础数据处理等功能，部分融入AI错题分析、知识点推送等模块，能够满足基础实验教学需求[15]。此外，国内学者在AI技术的本土化应用方面进行了探索，针对高中物理核心实验内容，优化AI算法与仿真场景，提升平台的适配性[16]。 在教学应用与研究现状方面，国内研究主要集中于两个方向：一是AI在虚拟仿真实验中的具体功能应用，如利用AI进行实验操作考核（自动评分、错误定位）、基于AI的实验教学评价体系构建、AI在实验预习与复习中的应用等[17]。例如，张磊等（2024）提出基于AI的物理实验操作自动评分系统，通过计算机视觉技术识别学生的操作动作，实现实验考核的标准化与自动化[9]。二是特定实验内容的AI辅助教学实践，如“电磁感应”“牛顿运动定律”“平抛运动”等重点实验的虚拟仿真设计与应用，探索AI技术在具体实验中的应用策略[5]。然而，多数研究停留在“技术工具使用”层面，对AI辅助虚拟仿真实验的系统教学路径探索不足，缺乏对课前、课中、课后全流程的一体化设计，且较少关注师生角色的适应性调整，导致技术应用与教学实践脱节[4]。

Lee, Padmanabhan, and Whang (1997) demonstrated that when companies in a supply chain make decisions independently, small changes in consumer demand at the retail store can turn into massive, unpredictable swings in orders by the time they reach the factory. This happens because each company relies on the orders from its immediate buyer to forecast demand, rather than looking at actual consumer sales. Because of this uncertainty, every company in the chain buys extra safety stock "just in case." This lack of coordination ruins efficiency because it ties up money in unnecessary inventory, and it hurts effectiveness because the wrong products are often in the wrong places, leading to stockouts. A coordination strategy called Vendor Managed Inventory (VMI) directly solves this problem. In a normal setup, a retailer decides when to order more stock from a supplier. Under VMI, the retailer shares its daily sales data and current inventory levels with the supplier, and the supplier takes on the responsibility of restocking the retailer's shelves. This creates a major improvement in efficiency. Because the supplier can see exactly what consumers are buying in real-time, they do not have to guess or rely on distorted orders. They can plan their manufacturing and trucking schedules smoothly, which lowers their operational costs and reduces the need for safety stock. At the same time, this coordination improves effectiveness. The supplier can proactively send products before the retailer even realises they are running low, ensuring that the end customer always finds what they want on the shelf. Coordination Example 2: Balancing Push and Pull through Postponement A second major way coordination helps supply chains is through a structural strategy called postponement. While VMI is about sharing information to manage inventory, postponement is about coordinating the actual manufacturing and distribution process to handle unpredictable customer preferences. Traditionally, manufacturers use a "push" system, where they guess what customers will want and mass-produce finished goods in advance. This is highly efficient because making things in bulk is cheap, but it is not effective if customers suddenly want a different colour or style, leaving the company with unsold stock. The opposite is a "pull" system, where the company waits for a customer order before making the product. This is highly effective for the customer, but very inefficient and expensive for the factory. Postponement coordinates these two ideas by delaying the final customisation of a product until the last possible moment (Swaminathan & Tayur, 1998). A great example of this is how house paint is sold. Instead of factories trying to guess how many cans of "ocean blue" or "forest green" paint to make and ship, they just mass-produce a generic white base paint. This is the efficient "push" part of the supply chain. The generic paint is shipped to local hardware stores. When a customer walks in and asks for a specific shade of blue, the store employee mixes the colour into the base paint right there. This is the effective "pull" part. By coordinating the manufacturing and retail stages around this strategy, the supply chain drastically reduces the cost of holding hundreds of different coloured paints (efficiency), while offering the customer an almost unlimited choice of colours in minutes (effectiveness).

Unlike traditional models where a retailer determines when to reorder from a supplier, in VMI the retailer provides the supplier with daily sales data and current inventory levels. This model increases efficiencies as the supplier has access to the most accurate data available regarding actual consumption. 1. Introduction

This study asks whether the existence of labor unions impacts the quality of goods produced, with product recalls used as an outcome measure and an indicator of product quality. Product recalls are an objective measure of product quality, as they are administered and regulated by government authorities. Unions can potentially impact product qualities through multiple mechanisms, including bargaining power, labor monitoring, and the degree of flexibility available to the workforce in producing goods. The exact nature of this impact is unclear and will be explored throughout this paper.

Studying the relationship between unionization and the likelihood of a product recall allows us to examine the relationship between labor-management relations and the operational output of the firm. This is important to study as product recalls entail significant costs for the firm, its customers, and the regulatory bodies tasked with overseeing recalls. We cannot simply use ordinary least squares (OLS) to compare unionized firms to non-unionized firms because such a method would not yield a causal estimate. There are two main reasons why this is so: (1) omitted variable bias (OVB); (2) reverse causality.

I therefore employ two methods to overcome these potential issues: panel fixed effects, which control for firm-level or industry-level factors that do not vary over time; and regression discontinuity (RD), which exploits a cutoff at 50% union vote share in order to compare closely matched firms that just barely won a union election with those that narrowly lost. Overall, I find a positive relationship between unionization and the occurrence of future product recalls when controlling for industry fixed effects in panel fixed effects models and in many of the RD specifications. Nevertheless, these results become less clear under the inclusion of firm fixed effects, and the point estimates are imprecise and sensitive to the choice of bandwidth under RD. Given the uncertainty surrounding the exact magnitude of the causal impact, I consider these findings suggestive.

2. Data, Measurement, and Causal Challenges
2.1 Data and key variables

I utilize two separate datasets compiled by Koen Vermeulen, Jonathan Scharff, Daniel Simcoe, and Michael Siemer (KSSS). The first is a firm-year panel that spans from 2003-2013 and contains 38,105 observations, including a measure of unionization, future product recalls, and several firm-level covariates. The second is a union election dataset containing 1,144 union certification elections, and includes the percentage of votes received by the union in the election, whether the union won the election, and indicators for industry and year. I use this dataset to measure cumulative product recalls in the years following the union election. I keep the datasets separate because the firms are identified by different identifiers in each file.

I measure the outcome, cumulative product recalls, in 1, 2, and 3 year windows after the election. For the panel fixed effects models, I treat unionization as a binary variable, as well as a continuous variable representing the percentage of workers in a firm represented by a union. In the RD models, I treat unionization as a binary variable and use the union vote share as the running variable, centered at 50%. I control for a variety of firm-level covariates in the panel models, including leverage, research and development (R&D) spending, market concentration, number of suppliers, firm size, productivity, and degree of vertical integration.

2.2 The causal challenges

The causal question in this setting is whether a firm that currently has fewer unionized workers would have more future recalls if it had more workers represented by a union (or vice versa). A simple OLS comparison of unionized firms and non-unionized firms would likely not identify a causal effect due to two sources of endogeneity.

First, there is the possibility of OVB. Prior to the passage of a union, unionized firms may differ from non-unionized firms in a way that is also associated with the future likelihood of product recalls. The characteristics that were omitted in our regression become confounding variables. For example, firms with poor management practices may have a lower tolerance for product defects, leading to higher recall rates, but these same firms may also face more organized worker unrest and have a larger percentage of workers represented by unions. Such a confounder could cause us to overestimate the coefficient.

The second source of endogeneity is reverse causality. Unlike OVB, reverse causality involves the outcome influencing the treatment, and can also cause us to overestimate the coefficient. Recall that the data on product recalls occurs after the treatment. However, product quality problems in the past can cause workers to demand union representation in the present. These same quality problems can result in future product recalls, thereby creating a correlation between unionization and future product recalls, even though the causal impact of unionization is lower. Nevertheless, we should note that the direction of these biases can change depending on the exact setting.
